title: Dust characterization of halos: The extended emission in protoplanetary disks
question: What is the nature and origin of faint, extended dust continuum emission (the 'Halo') in the outer regions of the protoplanetary disks Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau?

evidence.quote: Some of the observations taken directly from previously published works are: Elias 2-24 from (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L) and (cite: carvalho2024) (2017.1.01330.S, 2018.1.01198.S); IM Lup from (cite: oberg2021) (2018.1.01055.L), (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L), and (cite: careno2024) (2019.1.01357.S); and DM Tau from (cite: teague2025) (2021.1.01123.L).

what.value: Disk inclination and position angles for Elias 2-24 (29.0°, 45.7°), IM Lup (47.5°, 144.5°), and DM Tau (36.0°, 155.6°)

evidence.quote: Specifically, we adopted an inclination angle and position angle of 29.0°and 45.7°for Elias 2-24, 47.5°and 144.5°for IM Lup (cite: dsharp2), and 36.0°and 155.6°for DM Tau (cite: curone2025), respectively.

what.value: Stellar luminosities for Elias 2-24 (6.03 +/- 2.88 L_odot), IM Lup (2.57 +/- 1.23 L_odot), and DM Tau (0.36 +/- 0.18 L_odot)

evidence.quote: We assume a Gaussian distribution for $L_\ast$, centered at 6.03 $L_\odot$, 2.57 $L_\odot$, and 0.36 $L_\odot$ for Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau, respectively, following (cite: andrews2018) and (cite: jun2021).

what.value: Gas surface density profiles, scale radius R_c, power-law index, and disk gas masses for Elias 2-24 (0.038 M_odot), IM Lup (0.106 M_odot), and DM Tau (0.057 M_odot)

evidence.quote: For Elias 2-24, we assume a total gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 and adopt the scale radius $R_\mathrm{c}$ and power law index from (cite: pinte2023).
For IM Lup and DM Tau, we utilize the $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}$ derived from dynamical gas mass estimates by (cite: martire2024) (with vertical stratification) and (cite: longarini2025), respectively.

what.value: Stellar masses for Elias 2-24 (0.78 M_odot), IM Lup (1.19 M_odot), and DM Tau (0.47 M_odot)

evidence.quote: For Elias 2-24, IM Lup and DM Tau, we adopt $M_{\star}$ of 0.78$^{+0.34}_{-0.13}$, 1.19$^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, and 0.47$^{+0.014}_{-0.015}$ M$_{\odot}$, respectively (cite: andrews2018; martire2024; longarini2025).

what.value: Disk age estimates for Elias 2-24 (0.08 - 0.5 Myr), IM Lup (0.9 - 1.3 Myr), and DM Tau (2.9 - 6 Myr)

evidence.quote: We obtain $t_\mathrm{drift} = 8 \times 10^{3}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 3 \times 10^{4}$ yr, both 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 0.08 - 0.5 Myr (cite: andrews2018).

The corresponding timescales are $t_\mathrm{drift} = 6 \times 10^{4}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 3 \times 10^{4}$ yr, both approximately 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 0.9 - 1.3 Myr (cite: avenhaus2018).

The inferred timescales are $t_\mathrm{drift} = 8 \times 10^{4}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 10^{4}$ yr, are again 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 2.9 - 6 Myr (cite: garufi2024).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, align, and image multiwavelength ALMA continuum data
recipe.method: Flag +/- 25 km s^-1 around lines, average to 125 MHz channels, align phase centers via Gaia DR3 and fixplanets, perform iterative phase and amplitude self-calibration, and image with tclean (mtmfs or multiscale) followed by uv-tapering and imsmooth to common beam sizes.
key_parameters: channel width = 125 MHz, line flagging = +/- 25 km s^-1
image size = 10", pixel size = 1/10 of highest-resolution beam, multiscale scales = 0, 2, 6, 12 times beam

recipe.goal: Extract radial intensity, brightness temperature, and spectral index profiles, and measure disk sizes and halo fluxes
recipe.method: Deproject images using literature inclination and PA, azimuthally average in radial annuli, compute brightness temperature using the full Planck function, compute spectral index profiles, and integrate flux densities to determine R_68, R_90, R_99 and halo flux.
key_parameters: Halo starting radii: 86 au (Elias 2-24), 150 au (IM Lup), 130 au (DM Tau); outer boundary at 3 sigma_I of least sensitive observation (150, 300, 300 au)
assumptions: Inclination and PA: (29.0°, 45.7°) for Elias 2-24, (47.5°, 144.5°) for IM Lup, (36.0°, 155.6°) for DM Tau

recipe.goal: Perform multiwavelength radial SED fitting to infer dust properties and select dust composition
recipe.method: Fit 1D vertically isothermal slab model with scattering independently at each radial step (from r = 11 au outward in steps of 1/3 smoothed beam) for four dust compositions using MCMC, apply double-resolution fitting for Elias 2-24 and DM Tau, compare models via Bayes factors, and integrate Sigma_d to obtain total and halo dust masses.
key_parameters: 32 walkers, 5000 steps after 1000 burn-in steps, repeated a second time around median values; radial step = 1/3 smoothed resolution starting from r = 11 au
assumptions: Power-law grain size distribution n(a) propto a^-q; Bruggeman and Maxwell-Garnett mixing rules for opacities; bulk densities 1.675, 0.503, 2.036, 0.611 g cm^-3 for the four compositions
Constant Sigma_d extrapolated inward from 11 au to 0 au for total dust mass calculation

recipe.goal: Compute gas-to-dust ratios, Stokes numbers, and dust drift and growth timescales
recipe.method: Combine inferred Sigma_d, T_d, and a_max with literature Sigma_g and stellar masses to compute gas-to-dust ratio (g2d), Stokes number (St), and drift and growth timescales (t_drift, t_grow), propagating uncertainties via 5000 bootstrap samples at each radius.
key_parameters: 5000 bootstrap samples per radius; turbulent viscosity alpha_t sampled uniformly in 10^-4 <= alpha_t <= 10^-2
assumptions: Hydrostatic equilibrium and isothermal vertical structure for gas pressure; total g2d = 100 assumed for Elias 2-24; dynamical gas masses for IM Lup and DM Tau
